conventions.convention: The background is a smooth, Hausdorff, second-countable, boundaryless Lorentzian four-manifold of signature (−,+,+,+), with an independent orientation and a supplied timelike field selecting the future cone. The inherited choice assumption is ACω.
Length coordinates use x⁰=ct; c, μ₀ and G_N are positive formal parameters. The sourced Maxwell convention is ∇ₐFᵃᵇ=−μ₀jᵇ, while matter exchange is ∇ₐT_mᵃᵇ=Fᵇ_c jᶜ.

Observers have g(n,n)=−1; matter velocities have g(U,U)=−c². In a positively oriented observer tetrad, F₀ᵢ=−Eᵢ/c and Fᵢⱼ=εᵢⱼₖBₖ. The spatial projection of the energy-current has stress-energy-density units; physical energy flux is c times that projection.
The dust ratio α=σ/ρ is defined by division only on the positive-density region. The optional Ohmic law q=χE_U, χ≥0, is an additional hypothesis.
DEC permits a future causal current or zero for every future timelike input. SEC is WEC for the trace-reversed tensor, without assuming Einstein's equation.

A C² curve has an interval domain with nonempty interior; coordinate derivatives through order two extend continuously to included endpoints, where derivatives are one-sided. Its acceleration is defined chartwise without requiring a smooth ambient velocity field.

load_bearing.statement: Defines the formal Maxwell tensor, dust and perfect-fluid tensors, observer contractions, sourced Maxwell equations, matter exchange and Einstein equation on the specified Lorentzian background. These are mathematical definitions and conditions, without physical adoption or solution-existence assertions.

The Maxwell tensor is symmetric, trace-free and satisfies WEC, NEC, SEC and DEC. Nonnegative dust satisfies all four. For perfect fluids: WEC iff ε≥0 and ε+p≥0; NEC iff ε+p≥0; SEC iff ε+p≥0 and ε+3p≥0; DEC iff ε≥|p|. Finite sums preserve each condition.

For C¹ densities with ρ>0 and C² future timelike U normalized by g(U,U)=−c², dust exchange is equivalent to mass continuity and ρa=σF♯(U). Under continuity, charge conservation is equivalent to U(σ/ρ)=0.

For the specified perfect-fluid tensor and orthogonal conduction current, matter exchange is equivalent to the longitudinal energy equation and rest-space force equation. Under q=χE_U with χ≥0, −U·f=χg(E_U,E_U)≥0; for q=0 it vanishes.

For every smooth manifold with affine connection and every chartwise C² curve on an interval with nonempty interior, the defined acceleration transforms as a tangent vector and determines a unique continuous vector field along the curve, including one-sided endpoint values.

Under the smooth Maxwell equations, matter exchange and the stated Maxwell-stress identity, the total-stress Killing current is divergence-free and obeys finite-chain flux balance with its side-flux term. Separately, for a supplied local potential, compensator and existing normalized C² Lorentz-force curve, m g(U,ξ)+q(A(ξ)−χ) is constant.

seams_checked.note: The symmetry theorem preserves the stress-divergence supplier's smooth F,j hypotheses, μ₀>0, homogeneous equation and negative source sign. Its cancellation uses −F^{bc}j_c=−Fᵇ_c jᶜ. The local curve clause is proved separately. The page's stale readiness wording is recorded as a concern.

The physical consumers retain positive-density restrictions, velocity normalization, optional Ohmic assumptions, exact fluid energy inequalities and finite side-flux terms. The symmetry consumer supplies the local potential, compensator and finite C² Lorentz-force segment required by the separate curve clause.

The WKB and weak-slow results use the stated geometry, curvature, SI and component conventions. The scaling result preserves the dust positive-density domain, quadratic electromagnetic stress scaling and exact observer energy density, without claiming a coupled-solution construction.

The counterpoised-dust result uses the same formal source sign, tensor normalization and ACω convention. It restricts divided dust conclusions to ρ>0, checks the undivided exchange separately at zero density, and invokes energy conditions only for nonnegative dust plus electromagnetic stress.
